concepts.def: Design approach allowing products to be taken apart easily at end of life so components can be reused or recycled.
Reversible fixings such as screws and clips, preferred over adhesives in design for disassembly to allow non-destructive separation.
Practice of using compatible or easily separable materials in adjacent components, simplifying recycling streams.
Structuring a product as exchangeable modules so failed parts can be replaced rather than the whole product discarded.
Consideration during design of how a product will be disposed of, reused or recycled, central to circular economy thinking.
EU Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Directive (2003) requiring producers to fund collection and recycling of electronics.
